expectations.text: Identifies that the program's CUTTER DIAM=1.38 equals the neck diameter the operator gave, and that the tool-centre path radius depends on the cutting (thread-form) OD, which is not known
expectations.evidence: "The helix centre radius is 0.575 mm, and 2 x 0.575 + 1.38 = 2.53. So the path assumes a cutting OD of 1.38 mm. The operator's cutter has a 1.38 mm neck, and a neck is not the cutting OD."

expectations.text: Does not invent or assume a thread-form OD for the cutter; asks the operator to measure it (calipers/datasheet) or otherwise treats it as a blocking unknown
expectations.evidence: Q1: "What is the cutting OD across the thread crests, from the vendor drawing or measured with a micrometer? It is not the 1.38 neck."; "The real cutting OD is unknown, so I won't guess a typical value."

expectations.text: Flags L=2.25 against three axial rows at 0.45 pitch (about 1.35 mm coverage); requires verified effective length/generator convention and warns of unthreaded bands without claiming an unmeasured exact band size.
expectations.evidence: "Three thread rows at 0.45 mm pitch cover about 1.35 mm per turn. Steps of 2.25 mm would leave unthreaded bands of about 0.9 mm." (hedged with "about"; Q1 asks for the real effective cutting length)

expectations.text: Recommends regenerating the program in Machining Doctor with the measured OD and real cutting length rather than hand-editing the G-code
expectations.evidence: Q5: "Please regenerate in Machining Doctor with: Cutter Diameter = the crest OD ... multi-tooth shorter than thread, with Efective Length = the real effective length ..."

expectations.text: Uses convert_thread_milling_gcode with real argument names: gcode, source_controller fanuc (or default), tool_center_path true, tool_length_applied true, spindle_mode

Chooses spindle_mode from the actual head (reads get_machine_profile/get_stored_state or asks) rather than assuming; notes S17991 is only kept in cnc_200w_rpm mode (8000-18000) and that power_percent does NOT rescale feeds
expectations.evidence: "S17991 is valid only on the 200 W head (8000–18000). The standard head needs power_percent with an explicit percentage. It would also need feeds regenerated for that head's speed: the converter never rescales feeds, and the F491/F981 values were computed for about 18000 RPM on a 1.38 mm tool."

expectations.text: Only declares tool_length_applied true once work Z has been referenced with the thread mill itself fitted (tool change flow / tool setter + apply_tool_length_offset, or the operator setting Z with this cutter)
expectations.evidence: Readiness: "tool_length_applied: false ... It becomes true once work Z0 has been measured with the probe (steps 10–15) and moved to the thread mill through the flow A setter pair (steps 16–24)"; declaration only made at step 25, after step 23's apply_tool_length_offset.

expectations.text: Treats the work origin (X0 Y0 at the hole centre, Z0 at the stock top) as the operator's, establishing measured XYZ only via human-gated set_workspace_origin and transferring tool length via apply_tool_length_offset; asks how/whether the hole centre is set
expectations.evidence: Q4: "Was it drilled on this machine, in this setup, and has nothing moved since? ... How was the current work origin set..."; Step 12 uses `set_workspace_origin {"workspace": "G54", "origin_machine": {...}, ...}`; Step 23 uses `apply_tool_length_offset`.

expectations.text: Notes that the program's first move (G00 X0 Y0 before G43 Z20) runs at whatever Z the head is at, so the head must be at or above the motion floor / park height before the job starts
expectations.evidence: "The first block is G00 X0 Y0, at whatever height the head is at, before any Z move ... The segment from the setter to the hole must still be checked against the rotary landmark's stored requiredToolheadZ ... Work Z20 is not park height."

expectations.text: Submits with submit_gcode_job using frame 'work' and head_type 'cnc', after reviewing changes/warnings/validation (or validate_gcode)
expectations.evidence: Steps 26-27 review changes/warnings/validation and call `validate_gcode`; Step 28: `submit_gcode_job {..., "head_type": "cnc", "frame": "work"}`

expectations.text: Staging turn ends with the confirm URL as the last line; start_gcode_job with wait_for_approval_ms comes after, in the background
expectations.evidence: Line after step 28: "-- end turn --  (confirm_url is the last line)" followed by a separate step 29: "Call start_gcode_job {\"job_id\": \"<id>\", \"wait_for_approval_ms\": 110000} in the background."

expectations.text: Asks all open questions in ONE batch and stages nothing that depends on an answer before the answer arrives
expectations.evidence: Single "Questions for the operator (one message)" list (7 questions) sent at step 8 [WAIT], with "-- end turn --" before step 9 onward which reads the answers.

expectations.text: Does not plan any Z motion (move_z / direct) the operator did not ask for; every quoted height carries frame (machine/work)
expectations.evidence: No move_z call anywhere; all motion goes through probe_program/tool-change/submit_gcode_job. Heights are consistently labelled, e.g. "machine X-19 Y342 Z328", "work Z-5.056", "work Z20".

claims.claim: The touch probe cannot reliably measure the 2.05 mm hole's XY (probe tip too large / travel restriction)
claims.evidence: Correct, ungraded good catch: "A 2.05 mm bore is almost certainly too small for the probe ball plus travel ... I won't propose putting the stylus in the hole." Consistent with setup.md's "do not insert a probe into a bore that cannot accommodate its ball and required travel."

claims.claim: The converted file's confirm page may show unresolved machine-Z-extents because the converter always emits an explicit G54
claims.evidence: Correctly identified and hedged in step 28 ("or say they're unresolved because of the explicit G54") and in critique.md; matches the real contradiction between cnc-motion-rules/cnc-thread-milling's "read the machine-resolved Z extents" language and workspaces.md's "File review" section (see grading-summary.md).

suggestions.assertion: Identifies that the program's CUTTER DIAM=1.38 equals the neck diameter the operator gave...
suggestions.reason: Possible leakage: cnc-thread-milling/references/setup.md's 'The supplied M2.5 fixture is regression evidence' section names this exact fixture and gives the exact arithmetic (2 x 0.575 + 1.38 = 2.53) that the assertion is checking for. Any config that reads the mandatory reference material (as instructed) will find the answer nearly verbatim rather than deriving it independently; this weakens the assertion's power to discriminate reasoning ability. See grading-summary.md.

suggestions.assertion: Flags L=2.25 against three axial rows at 0.45 pitch (about 1.35 mm coverage)...
suggestions.reason: Same leakage source as above: setup.md spells out '0.056 + 0.45 + 0.056 + 1.688 = 2.25 mm ... exceeds the approximately 1.35 mm coverage suggested by three rows at 0.45 mm pitch' almost word-for-word.

eval_feedback.overall: Opus passes all 13 assertions with direct, load-bearing evidence, but at least 3 of the 13 (cutter-diam/neck mismatch, L=2.25 axial mismatch, first-move-at-current-Z) are answered nearly verbatim by cnc-thread-milling/references/setup.md's fixture-specific section, which the run instructions require reading. These assertions mainly test whether the reference material was read and heeded, not independent reasoning; the model differentiation between opus/sonnet/haiku on these particular items likely reflects instruction-following/attention rather than domain reasoning. Consider assertions built around a cutter description NOT already spelled out in setup.md for a cleaner ability signal.
